adjudicator: third pass for the #2140 items: claude-opus-5-5 through `claude -p`, no tools, no MCP server, no settings sources, run from an empty directory; given policy-v1 and each disagreement with the two labels in a seeded random A/B order (seed 21403, labelling/2140/adjudication-prompt.txt). It was not told which labeller wrote which label, was told to favour neither, and was allowed to answer "unsettled"; it settled every pair.

disagreements.reason: The item governs a password set at account creation ('initial user password min length of 12'), which is squarely PA-04's 'account registration' case. It specifies only HTML5 length and complexity checks and says nothing about screening against a common-password list.
disagreements.businessFact: Is the initial user password entered during setup checked against a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords that meet the 12-character policy?

disagreements.reason: The item is about the portal's password-change flow and requires that 'changing passwords' work without the spurious new-username step. That explicitly preserves the user's ability to change their password, so the rule clearly applies and is met.

A 'one time login link' that can be copied and emailed has to carry the login secret in the link itself, i.e. in the URL. DP-01 forbids sensitive information such as tokens in the URL or query string.

Staff create the patient's portal credentials 'from MRD', and the forced change is what stops staff from knowing the patient's password. A flag to 'prevent' that change lets the staff-set password persist, which is the situation PA-14 exists to prevent.

The bug concerns which email address the reset dialog displays ('should display the current email address'). It says nothing about how reset credentials are generated or when they expire, so attaching PA-12 is a stretch.

consistencyPass.why: Run in #2140, after arms had run on this set (it is a tuning set): adjudication saw only the cells the two labellers disagreed on, so a rule both labellers skipped on a requirement was never checked. governing-03's labels hold the pairs #2140 is about (a blocklist rule on flows that set a password) only because its consistency pass added them, and this set had none. So governing-03's procedure was run here, on the counterparts of its cross-cutting rules: PA-04 (blocklist on registration or change, for PW-07), PA-10 (multi-factor access, for TS-09) and AZ-01 (function-level access, for TS-01). TS-06 (audit) has no single counterpart (this policy splits logging into five narrower rules) and AS-02 (password procedures) none. Two tool-less claude-opus-5-5 sessions per rule were given the policy and all 33 requirements and asked about that one rule alone, on every requirement (labelling/2140/consistency-prompt.txt in id order for pass 1; consistency-prompt-pass2.txt, the same text in a seeded order, seed 21404, for pass 2). They saw no label, no rule summary and no arm.
consistencyPass.decisionRule: A standing label changes only when both blind passes agree on the new label. A cell the passes split on keeps its standing label.

changes.reason: Requests a forced password change at first login but does not say how the new password is validated.
changes.businessFact: Will the new password chosen at the forced first-login change be checked against a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords?

changes.reason: Redesigns the portal password update flow but is silent on checking new passwords against common passwords.
changes.businessFact: Will the redesigned portal password update reject passwords found in a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords?

changes.reason: Proposes a one-time auto-login link that takes the patient straight into the portal using only that link, which bypasses multi-factor access.
Adds a function to generate and copy third-party one-time login invitations but is silent on who is permitted to use it.
changes.businessFact: Which users or roles are explicitly permitted to generate and send third-party telehealth invitation links?
